name: Piperacillin-Tazobactam
summary: Antipseudomonal penicillin combined with a beta-lactamase inhibitor; broad IV empiric coverage for severe nosocomial and polymicrobial infections.
mechanism: Piperacillin is a broad-spectrum penicillin that inhibits penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs); tazobactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects piperacillin from hydrolysis by many beta-lactamases (including many ESBLs).

dosing.adult: 3.375 g IV every 6 hours (or 4.5 g every 6-8 hours)

safety.lactation: Compatible — minimal excretion in breast milk
warnings: AKI risk when combined with vancomycin
Bleeding risk at high doses (antiplatelet effect)

clinicalPearls: Antipseudomonal + anaerobic coverage in one agent — a common ICU empiric choice
Combination with vancomycin is associated with higher AKI rates — consider alternatives when possible
good: Broad empiric IV coverage for severe nosocomial and polymicrobial infections.
bad: ESBL coverage unreliable at high inoculum; resistance pressure; AKI risk with vancomycin.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard infectious-disease/pharmacology references. Combination CAS omitted (not confidently known for the fixed-dose product); individual component IDs given.
